Danish

Etymology 1

From Old Norse lítt, a short form of lítit, the strong neuter of the adjective lítill (“little”) (Danish liden, lille), and with the stem lid- also coming directly from lit-i- (aforementioned lítit, as well as feminine lítil, accusative masculine lítinn).

Pronunciation

  • IPA(key): /let/, [ˈled̥]

Adverb

lidt (comparative mindre, superlative mindst)

  1. a little, slightly

Pronoun

lidt

  1. a bit, a little
